The site off Cumber Lane in Wilmslow is close to where the Lindow Man - a 2,000 year old bog body - was found in the 1980s. One councillor said he voted for the plans because the council did not "have a chance in hell of actually winning an appeal". Councillor Mark Goldsmith, who spoke against the plans, said councillors "get blamed but this is national policy in practice" while a local resident said the decision was "hugely, hugely disappointing". David Wilson, from Protect Lindow Moss, said there were "extensive reasons" to refuse the plans. She said she wanted to comment because of "immense concern for the precedent this application would set in terms of large-scale development on peatland". title: Work to restore Manchester's Chinatown archway underway

evidence_packet.title: Work to restore Manchester's Chinatown archway underway
evidence_packet.lead: The gateway into Manchester's Chinatown is in need of significant repairs, the city council says
evidence_packet.summary: The gateway into Manchester's Chinatown is in need of significant repairs, the city council says
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Work to restore Manchester's Chinatown archway underway - BBC News Image source, Manchester City Council Image caption, The Grade II-listed landmark was a gift from Beijing to the people of Manchester Published 1 hour ago Work has started on the restoration of a landmark archway in Manchester's Chinatown. The Grade II-listed feature was a gift from Beijing to the people of the city in the mid 1980s. The gateway into the city's Chinatown is now in need of significant repairs which is estimated to take two years to complete, Manchester City Council said. Councillor Mandie Shilton Godwin said while the arch will be missed during the work "rest assured it will be worth the wait". Image caption, The work on the archway was a "priority", said councillor Mandie Shilton Godwin The work is part of a wider regeneration of the Chinatown area. Improvements have already been carried out earlier this year to make repairs to the large pagoda, new bespoke benches have been installed, and works are planned within the month to make repairs to the smaller pagoda. Shilton Godwin, executive member for clean air, environment and transport, said the arch has been a focal point for the Chinese community in Manchester for generations and ensuring it remains standing proudly for years to come was a "priority". "We know the significance this area holds for many of our residents and that's why we are committing to further investment, ensuring that it's not only a top destination for tourists visiting Manchester, but a community that local people feel proud to live and work in." She added: "During this two-year project we know that the arch will be missed, but rest assured it will be worth the wait." title: Manchester 'historic gem' library in line for £6.4m revamp

evidence_packet.title: Manchester 'historic gem' library in line for £6.4m revamp

evidence_packet.summary: The Grade II* listed Portico Library in Manchester city centre dates back to 1806
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester 'historic gem' library in line for £6.4m revamp - BBC News Image source, Andrew Brooks Image caption, The Portico Library was built in 1806 By Richard Stead North West , Reporting from in Manchester Published 1 hour ago A Manchester library described as an "architectural gem" has been awarded a restoration grant of £6.4m which will see it open up all three floors for the first time in a century. The Grade II* listed Portico Library in the city centre dates back to 1806. The cash from the National Lottery Heritage Fund will help with urgent repairs, create new spaces and a bookshop featuring Northern writers and publishers as well as a kitchen where people can explore Manchester's food culture. Dr Thom Keep, the library's chief executive and librarian, said it was a "landmark moment" in Portico's history and the changes would give people greater access to its 25,000 books and archive material. Image caption, Dr Thom Keep said the award was a "landmark moment" in the library's complex history Keep told BBC Radio Manchester the money was a major milestone in the £12m Portico Reunited campaign to "reunite this extraordinary building and make room for people to discover, learn and create together". The architectural plans will provide people step free access to the building making it easier for people to enter and move around the library. Currently, the stairs limit access and the library only occupies the first floor. Keep believes there will be a huge rise in visitors, which currently top about 30,000 a year. He said: "We're expecting that once we reopen 95,000 people will come and visit the space per year." title: Prestwich road closed by third sinkhole in 10 years

evidence_packet.title: Prestwich road closed by third sinkhole in 10 years
evidence_packet.lead: The closure of Heywood Road follows the appearance of a third sinkhole on the same road since 2016
evidence_packet.summary: The closure of Heywood Road follows the appearance of a third sinkhole on the same road since 2016
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Prestwich road closed by third sinkhole in 10 years - BBC News Image caption, The sinkhole has been cordoned off and there are diversions in place By Richard Stead Reporting from in Prestwich Published 16 September 2026 Once again, a sinkhole has appeared on a road in a town in Greater Manchester - marking the third time the same road has been impacted over the course of 10 years. Heywood Road in Prestwich, Bury, has been closed, and traffic diverted, after two or three large cracks caused the tarmac to dip dramatically. It is the third sinkhole on the road within a decade, with one first appearing in 2016 and another occurring on the same street in 2023. The area has been cordoned off while the utility company assesses the site "to determine the cause". Image caption, A sinkhole has twice previously appeared on Heywood Road prior to the collapse this month - once in 2016 and again in 2023 The previous sinkholes, in 2016 and 2023, followed sewer collapses. A United Utilities spokesperson said: "We have engineers on site carrying out further assessments to determine the cause of the sinkhole and establish whether it is linked to any United Utilities assets." More than 900 people faced stays of such length in the month prior to a damning inspection. A warning notice has been issued over the triage system, the identification of sepsis and how those with mental health needs are cared for after the unannounced inspection in May, with "rapid improvements" called for. National guidelines state they should be done within an hour. By Haider Saleem Reporting from North West Published 16 September 2026 A mother who shook her two-year-old daughter to death will not have her nine-year sentence increased after Court of Appeal judges ruled it was not "unduly lenient". Morsal Mohammed Naim, 33, of Levenshulme, admitted manslaughter and child cruelty after her daughter, Omra Wali Jan, suffered a catastrophic brain injury and later died. The Attorney General referred the sentence imposed at Manchester Crown Court in February. However, three senior judges rejected the challenge, despite saying they would have imposed a longer term. Lord Justice Bean said the original sentence fell within the range available to the trial judge and described the circumstances of the case as "exceptional and extreme". Warning: This article contains distressing details Image source, GMP Image caption, Morsal Mohammed Naim was jailed for nine years after admitting manslaughter and child cruelty Omra, who was aged two years and three months, had suffered repeated abuse before her death, including burns caused by the metal of a cigarette lighter. Police were called to reports of an unresponsive child in Levenshulme on 30 November 2023. Naim initially told paramedics her daughter had choked on a biscuit. Before pleading guilty, she claimed Omra had choked, fallen and hit her head on a baby bouncer and that she had shaken her in an attempt to revive her. Doctors later found Omra had suffered a brain injury as well as other unexplained injuries, including burns, bruising and a fractured rib. The animal welfare charity is proposing to create what it describes as a "one-stop shop" from rescue to recovery for animals most in need on farmland close to Pennington Flash in Leigh, Wigan. The charity said up to 150 jobs would be based at the Mossley Hall site if approved. It has submitted a environmental impact assessment report, published on Wigan Council's planning portal, which has been commissioned ahead of a full planning application. The document states that an "integrated animal welfare, veterinary, rehabilitation and education campus" is proposed on land at Mossley Hall on Slag Lane, Lowton, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said. Part of the site is just 50 metres (164 ft) away from the Pennington Flash nature reserve. The 15 hectare site is made up of agricultural land, a disused railway embankment and woodland. The document said the development would include clinical veterinary and behavioural facilities, rehabilitation, training and rehoming provision and administration buildings. The report said: "The main building with veterinary services and staff offices, a ferret block and an electrical substation will be located in the central south of the site. "The campus will include a small animals block, a hay barn, cattery blocks and a foul drainage treatment plant." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Once again, a sinkhole has appeared on a road in a town in Greater Manchester - marking the third time the same road has been impacted over the course of 10 years Heywood Road in Prestwich, Bury, has been closed, and traffic diverted, after two or three large cracks caused the tarmac to dip dramatically It is the third sinkhole on the road within a decade, with one first appearing in 2016 and another occurring on the same street in 2023 The area has been cordoned off while the utility company assesses the site "to determine the cause" The previous sinkholes, in 2016 and 2023, followed sewer collapses A United Utilities spokesperson said: "We have engineers on site carrying out further assessments to determine the cause of the sinkhole and establish whether it is linked to any United Utilities assets."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Records show a hospital trust is "among the worst in England" for people spending more than 12 hours in the emergency department More than 900 people faced stays of such length in the month prior to a damning inspection The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has downgraded urgent and emergency care at Royal Albert Edward Infirmary in Wigan, Greater Manchester, after several concerns were raised over patient care A warning notice has been issued over the triage system, the identification of sepsis and how those with mental health needs are cared for after the unannounced inspection in May, with "rapid improvements" called for The trust said it was "working hard" to make improvements The NHS watchdog previously rated the urgent and emergency care and the medical care at the hospital - which was also inspected - as "good" but has downgraded them both to "requires improvement"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Transport bosses are warning of severe delays as a busy interchange and stretch of motorway is set to be closed for two weekends The Simister Island junction of the M60 Manchester Outer Ring Road will be closed - and the motorway shut in both directions to junction 17 (Whitefield) - on the weekends of 26 September and 10 October, National Highways said Simister Island, north of Manchester, connects the M60, M62, and M66 National Highways added the reason for the closure was to remove five overhead gantries that carried M60 signage, and together weighed about 450 tonnes. Stephen Gordon, 37, has been sentenced to a community order for three offences of making indecent images of children across three different categories Gordon, of Central Road, Partington in Trafford , pleaded guilty to the charges on August 28 and released on bail. He appeared at Manchester Crown Court this week (September 15) for sentencing The court heard police received notification from the National Crime Agency in May 2022 with alerts about incident images uploaded to Facebook. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham names 20 schools and groups in Greater Manchester given £1.4m boost in 'people power' The government funding is to build their own clean power projects Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 06:34, 17 Sep 2026 View 2 Ima Several schools and local groups in Greater Manchester will have access to a £1.4m pot to build and control their own clean energy supply. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Warning notice issued for Greater Manchester hospital 'Excessively long waits' for beds saw one patient wait 44 hours Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:00, 17 Sep 2026 Updated 06:45, 17 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Accident and Emergency Department, An NHS trust has been issued a warning notice after concerns were raised over emergency services at a Greater Manchester hospital The Royal Albert Edward Infirmary, in Wigan , was found by inspectors to be among the worst in the country for the number of patients spending more than 12 hours in the emergency department. In the month prior to the inspection, 253 people had a wait of 12 hours or longer – an av This included ‘excessively long waits’ for speciality beds, with one patient waiting 44 hours during the inspection. There were ‘significant’ patient flow issues ‘across the hospital’, healthcare watchdog the Care Quality Commission added Additional delays were found at discharge with the trust again among the worst for this, the inspection report continued. Late paperwork meant some patients missed transport and care package cut-off times, in turn delaying discharge itself CQC inspectors reviewed two hospital services during their visit – Urgent and Emergency Services and Medical Care. Both received a rating of ‘requires improvement’, the second lowest of the four possible ratings – down from ‘good’ at their previous inspection

evidence_packet.evidence_text: But in January 2024 a new, single yellow line was painted along the road, prohibiting parking between 8pm and 8am Spotting the potential for problems, ParkAppeal sent a Freedom of Information request to Manchester Council to find out how many unwitting drivers had been caught out View 5 Images They discovered that this tiny road alone has earned the town hall up to £724,000 in just three years. In just three years, 22,606 penalty charge notices (PCNs) have been dished out to motorists caught out by the new arrangements, resulting in fines totalling £733,9 It equates to fines worth £670 each day. It means St John Street is - by some distance - the worst street in Manchester for parking fines Thousands have been caught out with many criticising Manchester Council, which makes around £7m a year from parking fines across the borough. Town hall bosses have defended the number of fines on St John Street, insisting there is plentiful and clear signage alerting motorists to Some motorists claim the new arrangement is confusing as pay machines on the street mention no ban. Some drivers say they have only spotted signs confirming the prohibition after being stung with a £70 fine, reduced to £35 if paid promptly

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Man who downloaded vile images of children given community order Stephen Gordon received an 18 month community order and a sexual harm prevention order News Hope Gallagher 07:01, 17 Sep 2026 View Image Manchester Crown Court, Crown Square A man who downloaded pornographic images of children as young as three years old has been sentenced. Stephen Gordon, 37, has been sentenced to a community order for three offences of making indecent images of children across three different categories Gordon, of Central Road, Partington in Trafford , pleaded guilty to the charges on August 28 and released on bail. He appeared at Manchester Crown Court this week (September 15) for sentencing The court heard police received notification from the National Crime Agency in May 2022 with alerts about incident images uploaded to Facebook. evidence_packet.lead: Wigan Warning notice issued for Greater Manchester hospital 'Excessively long waits' for beds saw one patient wait 44 hours Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:00, 17 Sep 2026 Updated 06:45, 17 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Accident and Emergency Department, An NHS trust has been issued
evidence_packet.summary: Wigan Warning notice issued for Greater Manchester hospital 'Excessively long waits' for beds saw one patient wait 44 hours Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:00, 17 Sep 2026 Updated 06:45, 17 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Accident and Emergency Department, An NHS trust has been issued
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Warning notice issued for Greater Manchester hospital 'Excessively long waits' for beds saw one patient wait 44 hours Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:00, 17 Sep 2026 Updated 06:45, 17 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Accident and Emergency Department, An NHS trust has been issued a warning notice after concerns were raised over emergency services at a Greater Manchester hospital The Royal Albert Edward Infirmary, in Wigan , was found by inspectors to be among the worst in the country for the number of patients spending more than 12 hours in the emergency department. In the month prior to the inspection, 253 people had a wait of 12 hours or longer – an av This included ‘excessively long waits’ for speciality beds, with one patient waiting 44 hours during the inspection. There were ‘significant’ patient flow issues ‘across the hospital’, healthcare watchdog the Care Quality Commission added Additional delays were found at discharge with the trust again among the worst for this, the inspection report continued. Late paperwork meant some patients missed transport and care package cut-off times, in turn delaying discharge itself CQC inspectors reviewed two hospital services during their visit – Urgent and Emergency Services and Medical Care. Both received a rating of ‘requires improvement’, the second lowest of the four possible ratings – down from ‘good’ at their previous inspection

A section of Heywood Road has been blocked off following the appearance of the huge hole on Tuesday (September 15) Locals worked together to place wheelie bins around the hole. The MEN understands GMP officers then placed cordons on the street to prevent motorists from driving over the crater In an update, United Utilities say engineers have begun repairing a collapsed sewer that created the sinkhole on Heywood Road. The road will remain closed for the foreseeable as the work continues This isn't the first time a the tarmac on Heywood Road has collapsed. In 2016, a massive sinkhole opened up on the busy street. In 2021 the Heywood Road and Bury New Road junction was closed for two days after another sinkhole appeared 2023 brought along more issues with a spate of smaller sinkholes reported near the junction with Bury Old Road. Maureen had previously attempted to climb out of the window and would throw items from the window on occasions Her family told coroner Jyoti Gill they had spoken to care home staff with safety concerns about the window, but nothing was done about it before her death on September 29 last year. Describing Maureen's death as a 'preventable tragedy', the family said: "She was an integral part The inquest heard how following Maureen's death, social care regulator the Care Quality Commission (CQC) has initiated criminal proceedings, but no further details were given. title: Death of worker at waste management company was 'accident waiting to happen', trial told as company, boss and colleague accused of manslaughter

evidence_packet.title: Death of worker at waste management company was 'accident waiting to happen', trial told as company, boss and colleague accused of manslaughter
evidence_packet.lead: Courts Death of worker at waste management company was 'accident waiting to happen', trial told as company, boss and colleague accused of manslaughter Anthony Elston and Jonathan Horan both deny manslaughter, as Mr Elston's company AMP NW Ltd denies c News Amy Walker Court report
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Death of worker at waste management company was 'accident waiting to happen', trial told as company, boss and colleague accused of manslaughter Anthony Elston and Jonathan Horan both deny manslaughter, as Mr Elston's company AMP NW Ltd denies c News Amy Walker Court report
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Death of worker at waste management company was 'accident waiting to happen', trial told as company, boss and colleague accused of manslaughter Anthony Elston and Jonathan Horan both deny manslaughter, as Mr Elston's company AMP NW Ltd denies c News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:34, 16 Sep 2026 The death of a worker at a waste management company was an 'accident waiting to happen', a jury was told as his boss, the company and a colleague went on trial accused of manslaughter John Graveson was killed after a Hyundai excavator, driven by machine operator Jonathan Horan, reversed over him at AMP NW Ltd at Aspire House industrial estate in Dukinfield, Tameside, in March 2023 Picker Mr Graveson, 42, originally from Carlisle, was pronounced dead at the scene. Trial jurors were told the waste management company AMP NW Ltd - now Waste Solutions Mcr Ltd - owned by Anthony Elston and wife Fallon Elston, had 'no identifiable safe system in place' CCTV from the day showed workers and machinery regularly in 'close proximity', it was said, and vehicles were driving with 'no segregation measures in place' "The prosecution say this was an entirely avoidable accident," said prosecutor Alan Compton KC. "Because of the way the yard was being run by the company and Mr Elston, it was sadly an accident that was waiting to happen."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Plans revealed for £60m 'lifestyle' hotel in historic Manchester city centre building It could be a major transformation. Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 16:58, 16 Sep 2026 View 2 Images The plans would invol A historic Manchester building is set to be transformed into a £60m ‘lifestyle’ hotel based in the city centre Plans were announced today (September 16) for The Oliver, Curio Collection by Hilton hotel at the Grade II-listed Shena Simon Campus on Whitworth Street, a site which was formerly part of The Manchester College. It is a project which will be funded and owned by the family office A lifestyle hotel is a type of accommodation focused on ‘immersive guest experiences’ and local culture rather than a standard corporate offering, bosses leading the project said Oliver Cookson said: “Manchester made me who I am. This city gave me my work ethic, my ambition and my belief that anything is possible when you back yourself. I’ve always wanted to contribute to the city’s future while protecting the character and history that make it special “The Oliver will be a hotel that feels exciting, welcoming and full of personality, and partnering with Hilton and the Curio Collection brand on our family office’s first hotel venture is something I’m incredibly proud of.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Man who downloaded vile images of children given community order Stephen Gordon received an 18 month community order and a sexual harm prevention order News Hope Gallagher 07:01, 17 Sep 2026 View Image Manchester Crown Court, Crown Square A man who downloaded pornographic images of children as young as three years old has been sentenced. Stephen Gordon, 37, has been sentenced to a community order for three offences of making indecent images of children across three different categories Gordon, of Central Road, Partington in Trafford , pleaded guilty to the charges on August 28 and released on bail. He appeared at Manchester Crown Court this week (September 15) for sentencing The court heard police received notification from the National Crime Agency in May 2022 with alerts about incident images uploaded to Facebook. Gordon was not charged with distributing these images and stated that around that time his Facebook had been hacked Officers attended the defendant’s address on December 14, 2022, where they found two mobile devices which contained 32 indecent images of children. The images included an unclothed child on a bed, who was described to be aged between 3 and 5 years old Judge Recorder Lowe raised questions as to why the matter had taken so long to come to trial, with prosecutor Elizabeth Walker suggesting there were issues downloading the files from his phone and recovering the data. Ms Walker agreed there was an “excessive delay”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Warning notice issued for Greater Manchester hospital 'Excessively long waits' for beds saw one patient wait 44 hours Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:00, 17 Sep 2026 Updated 06:45, 17 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Accident and Emergency Department, An NHS trust has been issued a warning notice after concerns were raised over emergency services at a Greater Manchester hospital The Royal Albert Edward Infirmary, in Wigan , was found by inspectors to be among the worst in the country for the number of patients spending more than 12 hours in the emergency department. In the month prior to the inspection, 253 people had a wait of 12 hours or longer – an av This included ‘excessively long waits’ for speciality beds, with one patient waiting 44 hours during the inspection. There were ‘significant’ patient flow issues ‘across the hospital’, healthcare watchdog the Care Quality Commission added Additional delays were found at discharge with the trust again among the worst for this, the inspection report continued. Late paperwork meant some patients missed transport and care package cut-off times, in turn delaying discharge itself CQC inspectors reviewed two hospital services during their visit – Urgent and Emergency Services and Medical Care. Both received a rating of ‘requires improvement’, the second lowest of the four possible ratings – down from ‘good’ at their previous inspection

Maureen O'Callaghan had moved to Berrycroft Manor, in Romiley , to benefit from '24-hour care' at a cost of '£1,600 a week', her family told Stockport Coron But the inquest heard how the 78-year-old, who had dementia, 'went downhill' throughout her time at the home in 2025. Maureen had previously attempted to climb out of the window and would throw items from the window on occasions Her family told coroner Jyoti Gill they had spoken to care home staff with safety concerns about the window, but nothing was done about it before her death on September 29 last year. Describing Maureen's death as a 'preventable tragedy', the family said: "She was an integral part The inquest heard how following Maureen's death, social care regulator the Care Quality Commission (CQC) has initiated criminal proceedings, but no further details were given. The court heard how Maureen had been physically fit, and enjoyed walking and swimming, but as her dement John O'Callaghan, Maureen's son, said: "From being the mum we all knew and loved, this horrible disease just got a grip of her. evidence_packet.lead: Courts Death of worker at waste management company was 'accident waiting to happen', trial told as company, boss and colleague accused of manslaughter Anthony Elston and Jonathan Horan both deny manslaughter, as Mr Elston's company AMP NW Ltd denies c News Amy Walker Court report
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Death of worker at waste management company was 'accident waiting to happen', trial told as company, boss and colleague accused of manslaughter Anthony Elston and Jonathan Horan both deny manslaughter, as Mr Elston's company AMP NW Ltd denies c News Amy Walker Court report
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Death of worker at waste management company was 'accident waiting to happen', trial told as company, boss and colleague accused of manslaughter Anthony Elston and Jonathan Horan both deny manslaughter, as Mr Elston's company AMP NW Ltd denies c News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:34, 16 Sep 2026 The death of a worker at a waste management company was an 'accident waiting to happen', a jury was told as his boss, the company and a colleague went on trial accused of manslaughter John Graveson was killed after a Hyundai excavator, driven by machine operator Jonathan Horan, reversed over him at AMP NW Ltd at Aspire House industrial estate in Dukinfield, Tameside, in March 2023 Picker Mr Graveson, 42, originally from Carlisle, was pronounced dead at the scene. Trial jurors were told the waste management company AMP NW Ltd - now Waste Solutions Mcr Ltd - owned by Anthony Elston and wife Fallon Elston, had 'no identifiable safe system in place' CCTV from the day showed workers and machinery regularly in 'close proximity', it was said, and vehicles were driving with 'no segregation measures in place' "The prosecution say this was an entirely avoidable accident," said prosecutor Alan Compton KC. "Because of the way the yard was being run by the company and Mr Elston, it was sadly an accident that was waiting to happen."

evidence_packet.summary: But in January 2024 a new, single yellow line was painted along the road, prohibiting parking between 8pm and 8am Spotting the potential for problems, ParkAppeal sent a Freedom of Information request to Manchester Council to find out how many unwitting drivers had been caught out
evidence_packet.evidence_text: But in January 2024 a new, single yellow line was painted along the road, prohibiting parking between 8pm and 8am Spotting the potential for problems, ParkAppeal sent a Freedom of Information request to Manchester Council to find out how many unwitting drivers had been caught out View 5 Images They discovered that this tiny road alone has earned the town hall up to £724,000 in just three years. In just three years, 22,606 penalty charge notices (PCNs) have been dished out to motorists caught out by the new arrangements, resulting in fines totalling £733,9 It equates to fines worth £670 each day. It means St John Street is - by some distance - the worst street in Manchester for parking fines Thousands have been caught out with many criticising Manchester Council, which makes around £7m a year from parking fines across the borough. Town hall bosses have defended the number of fines on St John Street, insisting there is plentiful and clear signage alerting motorists to Some motorists claim the new arrangement is confusing as pay machines on the street mention no ban. Some drivers say they have only spotted signs confirming the prohibition after being stung with a £70 fine, reduced to £35 if paid promptly

He was serving a controversial indeterminate public protection sentence , having been jailed aged 17 for two-and-a-half years for attempted robbery The 32-year-old was released in 2022, having spent 13 years in prison, but was recalled the following year after failing a drugs test. On June 18 last year he was found hanged in his cell and died in Royal Oldham Hospital three days later Now Manchester North senior coroner Joanne Kearsley has raised urgent concerns about his death. In a prevention of future deaths report sent to the prison and the chief coroner Ms Kearsley wrote: "Upon finding Mr Hamer the prison officers did not cut the ligature for nearly three "It was heard that they panicked and were visibly distressed on finding Mr Hamer. They had undertaken their basic life support training years ago on their initial prison officer training."

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

LHV has a growing presence in Manchester and is actively recruiting fintech talent as it expands its UK operations and lending Hosted by Manchester-based investor and real estate business Shenton Group, the visit brought together leaders from the property, technology, finance and defence sectors to explore opportunities for greater collaboration between Estonia and the North West The programme included a tour of Sister, the 4m sq ft innovation district being delivered on the former UMIST campus, where discussions focused on supporting connections between Manchester’s fintech and technology sectors and Estonia’s internationally recognised digital economy. Colin Shenton, Chief Executive of Shenton Group, said: “Estonia may be home to just 1.3 million people, but it has built a global reputation as a leader in digital technology, fintech, cyber security and innovation. That’s it. No banking, work, or online shopping. You check it when you’re deciding what to do with a weekend or when something big is going on sale, and everything in it is somethin Rules and folders keep everything in the same place and still demand attention. A separate account changes when you look rather than where things land. Since 2001 and as recently as January the town’s politicians have seen a well-documented spate of petrol bombings: of councillors’ houses, councillors’ cars, and the cars of wannabe councillors. Famous among them is the 2021 petrol bombing o That was the day Oldham Council tried, and failed, for the fifth time running, to muster enough cross-party support to elect a new leader — a position left vacant by Shah since May after a three year stint. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The situation has prompted concern that people are being deterred from visiting local high streets Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Cash payments have been suspended at a number of pay-and-display machines across Altrincham and Hale after what Trafford Council has described as a sustained campaign of vandalism Notices have appeared on numerous machines in recent days informing motorists that cash payments are unavailable and advising them to pay using the RingGo app Trafford Council says a “significant number” of its machines have been put out of action by targeted criminal damage and that it is working with Greater Manchester Police to identify those responsible But the situation has prompted concern that people who cannot or do not want to use smartphone payments are being deterred from visiting local high streets – with particular concerns raised about older and vulnerable residents Hale Civic Society said Cecil Road car park was “noticeably quiet” when members visited at 11.30am today and questioned whether the problems with the machines were contributing to the lack of cars

evidence_packet.title: Alex Batty's new life and job since he was abducted by his mother
evidence_packet.lead: Batty, from Oldham, was declared missing by his grandmother in 2017, aged 11, after his mother and grandfather failed to return him from a holiday in Spain and instead moved to France He spent the following years in isolation before he was spotted by a delivery driver in December
evidence_packet.summary: Batty, from Oldham, was declared missing by his grandmother in 2017, aged 11, after his mother and grandfather failed to return him from a holiday in Spain and instead moved to France He spent the following years in isolation before he was spotted by a delivery driver in December
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Batty, from Oldham, was declared missing by his grandmother in 2017, aged 11, after his mother and grandfather failed to return him from a holiday in Spain and instead moved to France He spent the following years in isolation before he was spotted by a delivery driver in December 2023 in the foothills of the Pyrenees in the south-west of the country Batty, who is now 20, said his job at a waste management company had given his young family financial security It has been a whirlwind couple of years for Batty, whose teenage years were spent living as a nomad in France His mother, Melanie, who was not his legal guardian and was heavily influenced by conspiracy theories, told him to throw away his passport They lived off-grid and he did not attend school

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Morsal Mohammed Naim, 33, of Levenshulme, admitted manslaughter and child cruelty after her daughter, Omra Wali Jan, suffered a catastrophic brain injury and later died The Attorney General referred the sentence imposed at Manchester Crown Court in February. However, three senior judges rejected the challenge, despite saying they would have imposed a longer term Lord Justice Bean said the original sentence fell within the range available to the trial judge and described the circumstances of the case as "exceptional and extreme" Warning: This article contains distressing details Omra, who was aged two years and three months, had suffered repeated abuse before her death, including burns caused by the metal of a cigarette lighter Police were called to reports of an unresponsive child in Levenshulme on 30 November 2023

evidence_packet.lead: Daisy, a Jack Russell-Chihuahua cross, caught the attention of The Oaks landlady Jessica Murray on Monday evening at the Ramsbottom pub When Murray investigated, she found the missing cup in a storage alcove beneath a lift-up seat, alongside toilet rolls kept there Organiser Paul

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Daisy, a Jack Russell-Chihuahua cross, caught the attention of The Oaks landlady Jessica Murray on Monday evening at the Ramsbottom pub When Murray investigated, she found the missing cup in a storage alcove beneath a lift-up seat, alongside toilet rolls kept there Organiser Paul Jenkins told BBC Radio Lancashire Breakfast the trophy had been located late on Monday "What better place to stash such an important historical piece of plasticky tin," he joked The trophy had disappeared from the presentation table during Sunday's competition, meaning organisers could not hold the usual trophy-lifting moment at the end of the event Jenkins said he hoped somebody had moved it as a prank, although it was not known how it came to be beneath the seat

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fly-tipping offences could face tougher penalties under new plans from Manchester City Council, which is proposing to increase Fixed Penalty Notices (FPNs) for serious cases to the maximum amount Offenders caught committing fly-tipping offences will now face a £1,000 fine, an increase from the current £700 penalty. Those who pay within 10 days will be eligible for a reduced payment of £700, with the full amount payable within 14 days. The landmark decision is subject to a The move is part of a wider commitment to tackle environmental crime and support the ambitions set out in Manchester's new Fly-tipping and Litter Strategy, which aims to reduce fly-tipping incidents by a third by 2035 Residents have repeatedly said cleaner streets, well-kept parks and action on environmental crime as among their top priorities for the city. Fly-tipping continues to place a significant burden on council resources, drain public money away from essential services and impact the h In 2025-26, Manchester recorded 17,954 fly-tipping incidents, resulting in the removal of more than 5,594 tonnes of waste from across the city. A total of 992 fines were issued for waste deposits in the same period The strategy supports the aims of the council's Our Manchester Strategy , which sets out a vision for cleaner, greener and better maintained neighbourhoods

Charlotte Connell, of Nantwich Walk, Great Lever, pleaded guilty to fly-tipping at Wigan Magistrates' Court on Thursday, September 10. Waste linked to her address was found dumped on land to the rear of Nantwich Walk in March 2026. The waste consisted of a large quantity of household rubbish, including plastic storage boxes, a glass table, toys, a travel cot, refuse bags and shopping bags. During investigation, Ms Connell confirmed she had arranged for a third party to remove household waste from her property but was unable to demonstrate that it had been disposed of lawfully by a licenced carrier. The court handed her a one day custodial sentence and ordered her to pay costs of £432 and a victim surcharge of £26. Cllr Robert Morrisey, Bolton Council’s Executive Cabinet Member for Regulatory Services, said: “The case serves as a stark reminder that those who don’t dispose of their waste lawfully face significant consequences, including court action, fines, costs and, in some circumstances, imprisonment. "Fly-tipping blights neighbourhoods, damages the environment and places an unnecessary burden on taxpayers who ultimately have to fund the clean-up. "Residents have a legal obligation to check that anyone removing waste on their behalf is a registered waste carrier and to keep records of any transactions. “Anyone wishing to report fly-tipping can do so via the Bolton Council website or by contacting the council directly.” Disposing of your waste legally You have a legal Duty of Care to ensure your household waste is

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.lead: History, power and empire collide in Button Up!
evidence_packet.summary: History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei History, power and empire collide in Button Up!
evidence_packet.evidence_text: History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. evidence_packet.evidence_text: There’s a cruelty to Mike Rice, a wickedness. In this show Mike talks about doing psychedelics with his brother, an entanglement with a Spanish Sausage Dog named Nino, and many other such rotten adventures ‘ Ireland has yet another legendary comedian ‘ – Dan Nightingale Irish farmer’s son, and general Nasty Character Mike Rice is one of Ireland and the UK’s fastest rising comedy stars. Having started comedy in 2016 Mike has amassed a large online following from podcast and stand-up clips, regularly getting millions of views on various platforms Mike began stand-up comedy in Chicago, where within two years he was working regularly at the most prestigious clubs in the city, including The Laugh Factory. He has since returned home because his mother made him, and has been quickly rising in the Irish and European scene, play Mike brought his first solo show The Best Boy in Ireland to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival 2018, in what was a sold-out run, and performed that same show to sold-out rooms at the Perth Fringe Festival in 2019 As well as co-hosting Mike & Vittorio’s Guide to Parenting with Vittorio Angelone, and Big Mike and The Chief with Rob Moriarty, Mike has appeared multiple times on smash hit podcast Have a Word and released his first comedy special in October 2023

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport’s only Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant, Cantaloupe, has closed its doors – but the team have quickly pivoted to launch a brand-new concept in its place If Cantaloupe was simple Mediterranean small plates and great wine, Bar Caput is all cocktails, pizza… and still great wine The new concept from the same team behind the original restaurant is inspired by ‘the drinking and aperitivi culture of Rome’ The intention is that while Cantaloupe was a real destination restaurant – especially after earning a Michelin Bib Gourmand earlier this year – Bar Caput will be a more return-to-time-and-time-again neighbourhood haunt On the menu, you’ll find brilliant, bright cocktails, like the ‘Bicycle Thief’ made with gin, Campari and grapefruit, and the refreshing ‘Calindri’ (named after the legendary Italian actor) Then for the food, the bulk of the menu centres around Roman-style pizzas, with thin, crispy bases and fantastic quality toppings

evidence_packet.evidence_text: With the future of devolution, AI policy and regional growth firmly on the agenda, Manchester Digital Managing Director and UK Tech Cluster Group Chair Katie Gallagher OBE recently spoke to The Startup Coalition about what the next phase could mean for Manchester and the wider No From the potential impact of greater devolved powers in Manchester to the role of No.10 North, Katie explores how national and regional government can work more effectively with the tech sector - and why the North’s different tech ecosystems need to be better connected rather tha Greater devolution will be positive for Manchester’s tech ecosystem. It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The best industry experiences don’t just show young people what a career in tech could look like - they give them the opportunity to become part of it That’s exactly what Hippo helped create through their support of Manchester Digital’s T Connect programme, providing students with exposure to the industry, practical experience and the confidence to take their next steps into tech Hippo’s involvement began with a problem-solving session for T Connect students, where their team ran activities designed to encourage creative thinking, collaboration and approaching challenges in the way technology teams do every day Following this session, Hippo selected two learners - Ahmed Abdul Karim and Edu Samuel Manuel - to take part in a 36-day industry placement with the business The placement gave Ahmed and Edu the opportunity to work alongside Hippo’s teams from their Leeds office, contributing to projects for the Department for Education and gaining first-hand experience of working in a professional technology environment Throughout their placements, they were treated as members of the team, gaining insight into the full process of delivering digital products - from technical development and problem solving through to collaboration and communication

The people making the real decisions are out of reach, so the anger lands on whoever is closest: the pop star, the familiar face, the easy target. Join Jonathan Schofield Tours for a closer look at this breakthrough moment via the buildings tha Despite the earlier rail line at Stockton and Darlington, it was the LMR that proved rail travel had a future. One, it almost immediately made money. Two, it democratised travel. For the first time poorer people could travel regularly for a reasonable price, having a lasting effe But while the railways made travel easier, they also made the separation of the classes more pronounced, with commuter towns like Wilmslow, Alderley Edge, Sale and Cheadle Hulme spreading over farm fields. This led to a debate about the abandonment of the city by those who owed t The Railway Age got off to an inauspicious start with an angry crowd in Manchester protesting about the price of food and about the lack of representation. There was tragedy too, when William Huskisson, a Liverpool MP, was run down and killed by a train

It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Along with the likes of Enzo Fernández, Elliot Anderson, Iliman Ndiaye and Allan to name just a few, Bouaddi’s arrival helped add further lustre to what is a hugely exciting and new-look City squad forged under manager Enzo Maresca. Despite having been at the Etihad for less than a month, Bouaddi has already offered several tantalising and exciting first glimpses of his quality and vast potential. And in a special interview with City Studios to reflect on the 2026 summer window as well as looking ahead, Viana revealed how the Bouaddi deal had been one long in the making. “Since the beginning [we were obsessed with him],” Viana said. “We’ve followed him especially for the last year and we had a conversation with the President of Lille before the World Cup. “It’s a position that we thought we could have to be very decisive during this transfer window and Bouaddi was always the target. “We had a positive conversation with the President of Lille and then we had the opportunity to speak to him. “When you speak with him, you have more desire to bring that mentality to our building. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Man United latest: Four clubs 'target' JJ Gabriel transfer as Man United exit fear emerges Manchester United starlet JJ Gabriel has sparked a new transfer saga Comments Sport Jake Bayliss 05:30, 17 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Manchester United starl Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has requested to cancel his registration at the club in a shock development for the budding young star's career. The 15-year-old prodigy is yet to make his official first team debut but did feature for Michael Carrick's side during pre-seaso Gabriel has regularly trained alongside the senior squad following his outstanding performances for United's U18's last season, netting 26 goals in 29 appearances. He recently bagged a hat-trick against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League and appeared to have a clear pathway into the However, Gabriel's future is now in doubt after he submitted a request to have his registration cancelled, though United have yet to accept it. United still believe the situation can be resolved but the club's chances of keeping hold of their academy gem could be complicated as t As he is eligible for a European passport, Gabriel could potentially move to clubs on the continent , unlike British players, who must wait until they reach 18. Having used mostly the same group for back-to-back matches at Porto and United last week, the City boss is ready to s Pep Guardiola won five Carabao Cups in ten years and Maresca has been told that his job is to make sure the team is strong across all four competitions. Guardiola would often use the cups to rotate though and Maresca is planning the same Rico Lewis, Rayan Ait-Nouri, Nico O'Reilly and Vitor Reis are among the players who could come into the team, while Allan could also get his first minutes since signing from Palmeiras. Academy trio Ryan McAidoo, Kaden Braithwaite and Floyd Samba are also expected to be involved Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN!
